title: Oh Say Can You Stream: Unveiling Our Star-Spangled America 250 Lineup
summary: Netflix has a new docuseries, 'The American Experiment' and several new collections to ring in the United States' 250th birthday.
body_text: Oh, say can you see… America’s big birthday celebration on Netflix! The United States turns 250 this July, and by the dawn’s early light, we’re so gallantly streaming a new docuseries and several new collections to ring in this major milestone. The American Experiment , which debuted June 24, is a sweeping five-part documentary series that traces how the ideals of America's founders gave rise to a nation. Directed by Brian Knappenberger ( Turning Point ) and executive-produced by Tom Hanks, Gary Goetzman, Sarah Huisenga and Knappenberger, the series features a wide range of voices including former vice presidents and cabinet officials, current and former members of Congress, a former Supreme Court justice, leading historians, tribal chiefs, military experts, and thought leaders across the political spectrum. (Check out some of the biggest moments from the series here .) Casting a wide net across America In addition to these familiar faces, we also enlisted former TV president Martin Sheen to voice the nation’s first president, George Washington. To narrate the series’ many other reenactments, we brought in more than 30 ordinary extraordinary Americans like firefighters, paramedics, police officers, military officers, historians, civil servants, and poet laureates. We also traveled from the mountains to the prairies to film these recreations, sending production to nine states across the US, including Arizona, California (near our headquarters in Los Angeles), Massachusetts, New Jersey (at our soon-to-be studio in Monmouth County), New York (near our studio in Brooklyn), Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Vermont, Virginia and, the nation’s capitol, Washington, D.C. Recreating historic battlefields using visual effects For many of these reenactments, we collaborated closely with our partners at Eyeline Studios . By combining fully generative work, volumetric capture, and hybrid generative/VFX workflows, Eyeline enabled everything from expansive ground and naval battles to richly detailed town and aerial shots rarely seen in documentaries. Previewing the series in our nation’s capital To celebrate The American Experiment , we hosted a special screening of the first episode at the Burke Theater at the US Navy Memorial on June 17. Presented in partnership with America250, guests included former Vice President Mike Pence (who is featured in the series) as well as members of America250, the DC America 250 Commission, the Military Women’s Memorial, the Smithsonian National Museum of American History, the Smithsonian Institute, the US Chamber of Commerce, the US National Archives and Records Administration and the White House Historical Association. The screening was followed by a Q&A with Knappenberger; Joanne Freeman, professor of history at Yale University and author of Affairs of Honor ; and moderator Sara Georgini, series editor for The Papers of John Adams and author of Household Gods . Although Knappenberger said he came up with the idea for The American Experiment two years ago, the 250-year anniversary provided the perfect opportunity to dive deeper into the country’s origin story. “I have to say, it was more moving, more powerful, and more amazing even than I thought it would be when we first embarked on this,” the director said. “Getting into these stories and these figures and the tensions that gave rise to all of this, it felt fresh. Every turn of this story felt like something was prescient and relevant, and every time you learned something, you wanted to know more.” From left to right: Brian Knappenberger, Joanne Freeman and Sara Georgini speak onstage at ‘The American Experiment’ Special Screening at the US Navy Memorial in Washington, DC. (Credit: Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for Netflix) Exploring America through curated collections If The American Experiment leaves you wanting to watch more about the land of the free and the home of the brave, we’re also launching several collections of original and licensed titles to celebrate the country’s birthday. In addition to our main collection, titled “ USA 250!, ” we’ve also put together 11 sub-collections that honor and amplify the full diaspora of American experiences and American stories, from blockbusters (“Lights, Camera, America!”) and westerns (“High Noon USA”) to food (“The United States of Food”), music (“The American Songbook”) and sports (“The American Playbook”). Explore middle America with “From Sea to Shining Sea” or dive deeper into US history with “250 Years of America.” No matter where you’re from or what you’re into, there’s truly something for everyone. (Find more patriotic title recommendations here .) And the fireworks — literally and figuratively — continue after America turns 250 on July 4th. Next up to the plate, we’re celebrating America’s favorite pastime with a live broadcast of the MLB T-Mobile Home Run Derby , taking place in America’s birthplace, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, on July 13 at 8pm ET/5pm PT. Check out The American Experiment and the “USA 250” collection — only on Netflix.

The webcast replay will be available on the Investor Relations website for 12 months following the event. From finding the best credit card to buying a house, NerdWallet is there to help consumers make financial decisions with confidence. Consumers have free access to our expert content and comparison shopping marketplaces, plus a data-driven app, which helps them stay on top of their finances and save time and money, giving them the freedom to do more. title: Scite Expands Extensive Publisher Partnership Network With American Society For Microbiology Indexing Agreement
summary: Direct Indexing Agreement Joins Over 30 Publisher Relationships, Setting Scite Apart With Most Comprehensive Publisher Network For Researchers In Competitive AI Landscape
body_text: Direct Indexing Agreement Joins Over 30 Publisher Relationships, Setting Scite Apart With Most Comprehensive Publisher Network For Researchers In Competitive AI Landscape HENDERSON, Nev., June 18, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Research Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: RSSS), a leading provider of AI-powered scientific research tools, announces that its Scite platform has signed an indexing agreement with the American Society for Microbiology (ASM), the world's oldest and largest organization of microbiologists. Under this agreement, content from ASM's comprehensive portfolio of peer-reviewed journals will be indexed and analyzed by Scite's Smart Citations technology, providing researchers with unprecedented insight into how microbiology research is being cited and utilized across the scientific community. This partnership adds ASM's prestigious journal portfolio to Scite's extensive network of publisher relationships—a key differentiator that sets Scite apart from other AI research platforms. While many AI companies operate without direct publisher partnerships, Scite has cultivated content agreements with more than 30 major publishers, enabling access to over 1.3 billion indexed citations from full-text scientific articles. Scite, in combination with Article Galaxy, helps researchers discover and access content, driving publishers' traffic and revenue. In fact, publishers with a Scite indexing agreement see an 11% increase in document supply revenues and experience approximately 2.5x more views per 1,000 articles than non-indexed partners. "The American Society for Microbiology has been at the forefront of microbiological research for over a century, publishing some of the most influential work in the field," said Josh Nicholson, Chief Strategy Officer of Research Solutions. "By integrating ASM's journals into our Smart Citations platform, we're providing researchers with deeper insights into how microbiology research builds upon previous work, whether it supports or contrasts existing findings, and how it's being applied in subsequent studies. This level of citation intelligence is only possible through our extensive publisher partnerships." Scite's Smart Citations provide rich contextual insights that traditional citation counts cannot deliver—extracting the specific sentences where references appear, identifying the section of the citing paper, and classifying whether the citation provides supporting, contrasting, or neutral evidence. This technology helps researchers quickly understand not just how often a paper is cited, but how and why it's being used by the scientific community. "We're thrilled to partner with Scite. Their innovative approach to citations brings a vital level of clarity and insight into how our publications are referenced," said Karie Kirkpatrick, Journals Platform Analyst at ASM. "They are transforming traditional metrics into a richer, more meaningful framework, helping ASM and our research community to better understand the scholarly impact of our work." The partnership will encompass ASM's full journal portfolio, including flagship publications such as Applied and Environmental Microbiology, Journal of Bacteriology, Journal of Virology, Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy, and other specialized microbiology journals. This content will join the existing citations already indexed by Scite from publishers including Wiley, The Royal Society, Wolters Kluwer, and many others. "What distinguishes Scite in the AI research landscape is our commitment to working directly with publishers rather than simply scraping content," added Nicholson. "These partnerships ensure that we're providing researchers with comprehensive, accurate, and ethically-sourced information while respecting publisher rights and supporting the scientific publishing ecosystem." The indexing agreement reflects the growing recognition of Smart Citations as an essential tool for modern research evaluation and discovery. Unlike traditional AI research tools that may lack direct publisher relationships, Scite's extensive partnership network enables comprehensive analysis of citation patterns across multiple disciplines and journals. About Research Solutions Research Solutions (NASDAQ: RSSS) is a vertical SaaS and AI company that simplifies research workflow for academic institutions, life science companies, and research organizations worldwide. As one of the only publisher-independent marketplaces for scientific, technical, and medical (STM) content, the company uniquely combines AI-powered tools—including an intelligent research assistant and full-text search capabilities—with seamless access to both open access and paywalled research. The platform enables organizations to discover, access, manage, and analyze scientific literature more efficiently, accelerating the pace of scientific discovery. About The American Society For Microbiology Established in 1899, ASM is the home for microbial scientists from around the globe to connect, learn, discover and prepare for the future. ASM and its over 37,000 members partner with global organizations to solve the world's most pressing challenges. We connect with millions of experts and harness their science to serve humanity. From climate change, antimicrobial resistance, industrial, basic and applied microbiology, ASM is a leader in scientific publishing, stands for open science and advocates for evidence-based public policies. For more information about Research Solutions, visit: www.researchsolutions.com | LinkedIn | Facebook | X SOURCE Research Solutions, Inc. For further information: Lydia Lindenberg, Director of Content Marketing, llindenberg@researchsolutions.com .

Building an Ideal Tech Stack for LLM Applications From Scratch
summary: Tutorials, guides and deep dives into the best techniques and research for building reliable AI.
body_text: Do not index Original Paper Blog URL Introduction As AI and machine learning rapidly evolve, the process of creating applications powered by LLMs has become both more exciting and challenging. In this blog post, we'll take you on a journey through the essential components and tools needed to build a robust tech stack for LLM applications from the ground up. Whether you're starting from scratch or looking to refine your approach, this guide will provide you with the insights needed to make informed decisions and unlock the true potential of LLMs. 1. Data Ingestion and Integration The first step in creating a robust LLM application is ensuring seamless data ingestion from various sources. Whether you're dealing with structured data from enterprise databases or unstructured data from knowledge bases, having the right tools is critical. Data Connectors & ETL Tools: Open Source: Apache NiFi : Excellent for automating data flows, real-time data streaming, and handling complex ingestion tasks. Airbyte : A powerful tool for extracting, loading, and transforming data from multiple APIs and databases. Closed Source: Fivetran : A managed service that simplifies data pipeline creation with minimal configuration. Stitch : A cloud-based ETL service designed for simplicity and ease of use. 2. Data Storage and Management Selecting the right data storage system is vital, especially when working with both structured and unstructured data. Structured Data Storage: Open Source: PostgreSQL/MySQL : Reliable relational databases with extensive community support. Closed Source: Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL/MySQL): A scalable, managed solution with built-in reliability. Unstructured Data Storage: Open Source: Elasticsearch : Ideal for indexing and searching large volumes of unstructured data. MongoDB : A flexible NoSQL database, perfect for handling JSON-like data structures. Closed Source: Amazon OpenSearch : A managed version of Elasticsearch, offering the same powerful search capabilities. Azure AI Search (formerly Cognitive Search): A managed service designed for sophisticated search applications. 3. Structured Data Extraction Converting unstructured data into structured formats suitable for AI applications is a crucial step in the pipeline. Tools for Structured Data Extraction: Unstructured.io : A platform that transforms unstructured data into AI-ready structured formats. Llamaparse : A versatile parsing tool from Llamaindex, supporting multiple file types and languages. GPT-4: OpenAI's cutting-edge model for extracting structured data from complex formats. 4. Data Preprocessing and Cleaning Before feeding data into your models, it must be preprocessed and cleaned. This ensures the data is in a usable state and improves model accuracy. Data Processing Frameworks: Open Source: Apache Spark : Handles large-scale data processing for both batch and streaming data. Pandas (Python): Excellent for manipulating and analyzing smaller datasets. Closed Source: Databricks : A cloud platform that builds on Apache Spark, offering advanced big data processing capabilities. 5. Open Source LLM Development Frameworks Selecting the right framework to build your LLM application is critical. Here are some leading options: Langchain : A popular framework providing standardized interfaces and components for LLM development. Llamaindex : Facilitates the connection of custom data sources with LLMs, making it easier to develop RAG applications. Haystack : An open-source framework for building production-ready LLM applications. 6. Vectorization and Embedding Models Vectorization and embedding models play a vital role in transforming text into meaningful vector representations for NLP tasks. Key Embedding Models: OpenAI's ADA-002: Known for generating high-quality text embeddings, suitable for various NLP tasks. Google's PaLM2 Gecko-001: Provides robust embeddings for deep semantic understanding. Hugging Face Transformers: A versatile library for generating embeddings using pre-trained models like BERT and GPT. 7. Building the Retrieval System A robust retrieval system is the backbone of any RAG application, enabling efficient information retrieval. Vector Databases: Open Source: FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search): A tool for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors. Milvus : A scalable, high-performance vector database. Closed Source: Weaviate : A cloud-native vector search engine, perfect for AI applications requiring high-dimensional vector handling. Qdrant : An open-source vector database optimized for high-performance similarity search. 8. Building the Generation System (LLMs) The generation system is where the magic happens—creating meaningful text responses based on retrieved information. LLM Fine-Tuning: Open Source: Hugging Face Transformers : Enables fine-tuning of pre-trained models on specific datasets. Llama Factory : Provides a UI for enhanced and efficient model fine-tuning. Closed Source: Amazon SageMaker : A managed environment for fine-tuning and deploying LLMs. Replicate : Supports the fine-tuning and deployment of custom models. Open Pipe : Known for its high-speed model fine-tuning and deployment. Model Deployment: Open Source: Hugging Face Inference API : Deploy custom or pre-trained models easily. FastAPI or Flask: Serve machine learning models as APIs. Closed Source: Azure OpenAI Service: Deploy models like GPT-4 in a managed environment. Google Vertex AI : A scalable platform for deploying large models. Groq : Known for its high-speed AI inference technology. 9. Experimentation with AI Pipelines Experimenting with different pipelines and model variations is crucial for optimizing performance. Athina IDE : A collaborative platform that enables running and evaluating experiments rapidly, with a focus on both technical and non-technical users. MLflow : A powerful open-source tool for managing the entire machine learning lifecycle, from experimentation to deployment. 10. Open-Source Evaluation Frameworks Evaluating your LLM application is vital to ensure it meets the required standards and performs optimally. RAGAS : Provides a suite of metrics for evaluating various aspects of RAG systems. DeepEval : Facilitates unit testing of LLM outputs in Python, including regression testing and hyperparameter discovery. Guardrails AI : Ensures your AI models operate within specified parameters through a comprehensive validation framework. 11. Monitoring and Evaluation Platforms Monitoring and debugging your LLM application in production is critical for maintaining its performance and reliability. Traceloop : An open-source monitoring platform built on OpenTelemetry, ideal for debugging complex AI applications. Langsmith : Offers comprehensive monitoring, tracing, and debugging capabilities specifically for LLM applications. Langfuse : Another open-source platform, providing detailed traces for monitoring complex LLM applications. 12. Deployment and Scaling Finally, deploying and scaling your LLM application requires the right tools to ensure it can handle production workloads efficiently. Containerization: Docker : Containerize your application components for portability and ease of deployment. Kubernetes : Orchestrate containerized applications for scalability and reliability. CI/CD: Open Source: Jenkins : Automate your CI/CD pipeline for continuous integration and delivery. GitLab CI : Integrated pipelines for seamless code management and deployment. Closed Source: GitHub Actions : Seamlessly integrates with GitHub repositories for automating workflows. CircleCI : Provides scalable CI/CD pipelines with easy configuration. Final Thoughts A shoutout to our clients and ecosystem partners for their unbiased contributions to this resource. This guide provides a flexible strategy, allowing you to begin with budget-friendly, community-supported tools and seamlessly scale up with managed services as your project evolves. By carefully choosing the right mix of technologies, you can build an LLM application that is both powerful and scalable, perfectly suited to meet the demands of today's AI-driven landscape. Is there something we missed? We'd love to hear from you! :) 💡 We regularly create and crowdsource valuable articles for our community. Check out AI Hub
